function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability** | Goal | What Turbonomics Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across Clouds** | • A single pane of glass that aggregates metrics from GCP, AWS, Azure, on‑prem, and edge environments.
• Real‑time dashboards with AI‑driven anomaly detection. | Unilever can see the health of all workloads—whether they’re running on Google Kubernetes Engine, Amazon ECS, or Azure VMs—without switching consoles. | | **Predictive Capacity Planning** | • Machine‑learning models that forecast CPU, memory, storage, and network usage based on historical trends and upcoming releases.
• Automated “what‑if” simulations for scaling decisions. | Enables proactive scaling of marketing analytics, supply‑chain simulations, and e‑commerce sites before traffic spikes hit. | | **Cost Optimization & Chargeback** | • AI‑based cost attribution per business unit, product line, or campaign.
• Automated budget alerts and policy enforcement. | Helps Unilever keep cloud spend in check while ensuring high‑performance for critical consumer‑facing services. | | **Policy‑Based Automation** | • Declarative policies that enforce SLAs, security, and compliance across all clouds.
• Auto‑remediation of infra drift or misconfigurations. | Reduces manual toil for the IT ops team and ensures consistent governance across global regions. | | **Self‑Healing Workloads** | • AI‑driven root‑cause analysis that automatically re‑routes traffic or spins up new instances when anomalies are detected. | Minimizes downtime for Unilever’s global e‑commerce platform and reduces mean time to recovery (MTTR). | **Key Differentiators vs Native Cloud Tools** | Feature | Turbonomics | Native Cloud Tool (GCP, AWS, Azure) | |---------|-------------|-------------------------------------| | **Scope** | Cross‑cloud, hybrid, and edge | Single‑cloud only | | **AI/ML Core** | Proprietary ML engine that learns from multi‑cloud telemetry; continuously improves over time | Cloud‑specific analytics (e.g., CloudWatch, Stackdriver) that are largely rule‑based | | **Unified Policy Engine** | One policy language that applies to all clouds | Separate policy frameworks (IAM, Security Center, etc.) | | **Cost Attribution** | Fine‑grained, AI‑driven chargeback per workload, per business unit | Native cost explorer provides high‑level cost breakdowns but lacks AI‑driven forecasting | | **Automation** | Self‑healing, auto‑scaling, auto‑remediation across clouds | Cloud‑native automation (Lambda, Cloud Functions, Azure Logic Apps) but limited to that provider | | **Observability Depth** | Combines metrics, logs, traces, and AI insights into a single UI | Each provider offers its own stack (e.g., Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, Azure Monitor) but requires stitching together | | **Vendor Lock‑In** | Vendor‑agnostic; no need to rewrite policies when moving workloads | Tied to the specific cloud’s APIs and services | **Bottom Line for Unilever** Turbonomics gives Unilever a *single, AI‑powered lens* to monitor, optimize, and automate workloads across all its cloud environments. While each cloud provider offers powerful native tools, they work in silos and require separate dashboards, policies, and cost models. Turbonomics bridges those gaps, enabling Unilever to: 1. **Reduce operational complexity** – one console, one policy set, one cost model. 2. **Improve agility** – AI‑driven recommendations let teams react faster to market changes. 3. **Control spend** – predictive cost modeling and automated chargeback keep budgets aligned with business goals. By adopting Turbonomics, Unilever can focus more on delivering value to consumers and less on managing disparate cloud ecosystems.
